title: POC pilot scope & integration plan — Zenith Retail
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week proof-of-concept to integrate Redwood's OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints into Zenith Retail's recommendation and search pipelines. Discussed success criteria (latency < 100ms p50 for chat, <= 250ms p95 for short queries; embedding recall delta < 2% vs baseline), workload sizing for peak events, benchmark plan, SDK integration approach (OpenAI-compatible vs native SDK), function/tool-calling for inventory lookups, structured JSON outputs for downstream parsers, and security/VPC access. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send benchmark template, draft SOW and pilot test plan, schedule a baseline benchmark run w/c 2025-05-19, and provide temporary test creds + example SDK snippets.
topics: Success criteria: latency, cost, quality thresholds
Workload sizing: QPS, token distribution, peak day scenarios
Benchmark plan: datasets, perf harness, metrics to capture
Integration plan: OpenAI-compat endpoints, SDKs, streaming, function calling
Security & infra: VPC peering, SSO, data retention
next_steps: Redwood (Eli): Send benchmark template and perf spreadsheet by 2025-05-09
Zenith (Diego): Share sample production traces and token distribution CSV by 2025-05-12
Redwood (Priya): Draft 4-week POC SOW and pilot test plan by 2025-05-10
Schedule baseline benchmark run week of 2025-05-19 (tentative)
Set up temporary test credentials and sandbox VPC access (Zenith/Redwood ops)
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and finalize SLOs after run
action_items: Eli (AE): Email pricing tiers + token unit economics example (by 2025-05-09)
Priya (SE): Provide sample SDK snippets for JavaScript + Python (OpenAI-compatible) and a short demo app repo link
Diego (Lead ML): Export and send a 7-day token histogram and 24-hour peak minute QPS (by 2025-05-12)
Marcus (CTO): Confirm who on infra team will coordinate VPC peering and provide contact (by 2025-05-09)
Sonia (PM): Validate success criteria with stakeholders and confirm ROI metric to track during pilot (by 2025-05-11)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Eli Navarro (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO, Zenith), Aisha Khan (Head of Search), Diego Alvarez (Lead ML), Sonia Patel (PM)

[00:00] Eli: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Eli from Redwood, I'll kick us off — Priya's our solutions engineer. Quick agenda, scoping the pilot, success criteria, the perf/benchmark plan, and how you want to integrate — OpenAI-compatible endpoints or native SDK, function calling, structured outputs.

[00:20] Marcus: Great, yeah thanks. We want to move fairly fast. High level we have two consumer-facing flows: search/autocomplete and a recommendation assistant in our mobile app. We're concerned about latency on peak days — holiday spikes — and also keeping embedding quality high for personalized results.

[00:38] Priya: Quick clarifying question — when you say embedding quality, is that recall vs your current dense retriever?

[00:42] Aisha: Yeah, we measure recall@10 and want delta under 2% relative to our current Faiss baseline. Also embeddings feed into a reranker so small regressions amplify.

[01:05] Eli: Perfect. For the POC goal let's write down concrete thresholds: embedding recall delta < 2% absolute, and for generation/assistant latency targets p50 under 100 ms and p95 under 300 ms for short queries — what do you think?

[01:28] Diego: p95 300 seems okay for backend generation; for the search path where we do re-ranker calls we need lower p95 — around 250 ms max. Also need to define cost goal — we have an internal target of keeping per-1000-queries cost under $X (they left placeholder) — we'll fill in.

[01:50] Sonia: Timeline wise we're aiming to have a working pilot in 4 weeks, with bench runs and a stability week.

[02:00] Priya: That aligns with our standard POC cadence: week 0-1 integration and baseline collection, week 2 bench runs and tuning (quantization/caching), week 3 full regression tests and perf tuning, week 4 review and wrap with SOW for next steps.

[02:20] Marcus: How invasive is the SDK work? We'd prefer the OpenAI-compatible endpoints so we can swap in without a lot of code changes.

[02:30] Priya: Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible REST interfaces and SDK wrappers — same request shapes for chat, completions, embeddings. We also offer native SDKs with additional features around streaming and praformance knobs, but OpenAI-compat is usually fastest to adopt. There may be minor differences on function calling semantics and tool integrations depending on the client lib.

[02:55] Eli: We'll include example JS and Python snippets. For inventory lookups and to avoid hallucination, function/tool calling is a good fit — call out product detail service and return structured JSON so your parsers don't have to guess.

[03:15] Aisha: Right, we need strict JSON schemas back from the model for the assistant so downstream systems can ingest without extra heuristics.

[03:24] Priya: We can demonstrate Redwood's structured output enforcement — you can provide a JSON schema and we'll return model responses validated against it or fall back to a special error token. Note sometimes transcripts show 'schema enforcement' as 'schema enforcements' in our logs — little tilda.

[03:42] Diego: On the perf side, how do you handle batching and KV cache? In peak traffic we need high throughput and low latency.

[03:50] Priya: We have continuous batching with workload-aware policies and automatic KV cache reuse for prefix-heavy workloads — so if you have many similar session starts we keep the prefix state. We call it KV cache but sometimes it's transcribed as K V cash in our notes.

[04:10] Marcus: Security — we need SSO, SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration. Also VPC peering or private link for the pilot.

[04:18] Eli: All of that is supported. For Private deployments we can do VPC peering; for hosted we have private endpoints and customer-managed keys via KMS. We'll need your infra contact for peering.

[04:33] Sonia: One operational question: if the Redwood endpoint is temporarily degraded, do you offer fallbacks to smaller models or cached responses?

[04:40] Priya: Yes, routing policies allow fallbacks to smaller model variants, regional replicas, or serve cached completions. We can model that into the SLO testing.

[05:02] Eli: Let's talk benchmarks — Diego, can you give a sense of your token distribution and typical sequence lengths for search and assistant flows?

[05:10] Diego: Search queries are short — median 8 tokens, 95th at 24. Assistant sessions are longer: median 120, 95th about 420. But most assistant calls are multi-turn where we keep a trimmed context. Peak QPS on Black Friday last year hit 2,500 requests per minute for the search path — short queries — and around 300 reqs per minute for assistant.

[05:36] Priya: Excellent. For benching we'll ask for a 24-hour trace plus a 7-day histogram to synthesize load. We'll run microbenchmarks for p50/p95 across target seq lengths, and end-to-end bench including network latencies from your VPC region.

[06:00] Aisha: Are you able to run benchmarks inside our VPC or do we run a harness against your public endpoints?

[06:06] Priya: We can do both. For the closest-to-prod result we'll run the perf harness from machines in your cloud region via a private endpoint. Otherwise we provide a Redwood-managed bench with similar characteristics.

[06:20] Marcus: On observability, do we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency?

[06:26] Eli: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, latency histograms per model and per-route. We'll also provide traces and error logs for the pilot.

[06:38] Sonia: For the structured output, we need to validate shape and also capture parsing errors. Is there an automated report for schema violations?

[06:45] Priya: We can include violation metrics in the pilot dashboard and emit events to your logging stack. For the POC we'll include a small rule-based validator and sample failing cases so your product team can tune prompts or the schema.

[07:05] Eli: Let's capture success criteria explicitly in the SOW: 1) embedding recall within 2% of baseline, 2) search p95 <= 250 ms, 3) assistant p50 <= 100 ms and p95 <= 300 ms, 4) per-1000-query cost target (to be filled), 5) no more than X% schema violation rate (TBD).

[07:30] Diego: One technical note — our retriever uses FAISS + product embeddings. We'll need to compare Redwood-generated embeddings with our existing vectors and run a small A/B evaluation on a 10k query set.

[07:42] Priya: We'll prepare an embedding evaluation harness and Jupyter notebook you can run. We'll also share a mapping script for converting Redwood embedding vectors to your index schema.

[07:56] Marcus: Timeline and milestones?

[08:00] Eli: Proposed: Week 1 (05/12 - 05/16): integration + data share + baseline collection. Week 2 (05/19 - 05/23): run microbenchmarks and embedding eval; tuning. Week 3 (05/26 - 05/30): stress tests (peak QPS) and reliability checks. Week 4 (06/02 - 06/06): final analysis, dashboard handoff, and SOW/next-step decision.

[08:26] Sonia: That looks reasonable. We might push stress week earlier depending on infra availability but overall 4-week window ok.

[08:36] Diego: For integration, do you recommend using streaming for assistant responses to reduce perceived latency?

[08:42] Priya: Absolutely — streaming reduces time-to-first-token. SDKs support streaming chunked responses and partial function outputs. One caveat: some of our telemetry differs slightly in streaming mode so we'll want to include that in bench metrics.

[09:02] Eli: About function/tool calling — typical pattern is model returns a tool call intent, Redwood routes to your inventory service, and the function returns structured JSON back into the model or directly to your frontend. You'll want idempotency and safeguards on calls to avoid side effects during bench.

[09:24] Aisha: For safety, we will run bench in read-only mode for inventory and throttle calls.

[09:30] Priya: Good plan. Also we'll supply an example of function schemas and how to annotate required vs optional fields so the model is less ambiguous.

[09:45] Marcus: Any gotchas on model selection and quantization? We prefer cheaper variants if they meet quality bar.

[09:52] Priya: We'll recommend model families based on your quality targets and sequence length profiles. For production cost reduction we can test int8 or q4 quantized builds; sometimes you see minor quality tradeoffs for embedding tasks, so benching is essential. We'll include quantization recommendations in the perf report.

[10:14] Diego: When you talk about automatic caching, is it prefix-only or can you cache calls with similar arguments? We have a lot of near-duplicates in search suggestions.

[10:22] Priya: We support prefix and semantic caching for exact-match and near-match patterns; config is part of the pilot tuning. Our caching layer is TTL-based and tunable per-route.

[10:36] Eli: Let's call out the resource needs for perf runs: we might request ephemeral dedicated capacity for the stress test — that helps hit the QPS without affecting hosted tenants. That'll be in the SOW as an option.

[10:52] Sonia: Cost for ephemeral capacity — please include delta pricing so we can budget.

[10:58] Eli: Will do.

[11:05] Marcus: For auditing and compliance, we need to know retention windows and how to purge data.

[11:12] Eli: Hosted logs and transcripts are configurable; we can set short retention for pilot and provide immediate purge commands. For Private deployments, logs reside in your account with your retention policy.

[11:28] Diego: On credentials, we need a way to rotate test tokens and not expose long-lived keys.

[11:34] Priya: We'll issue short-lived sandbox tokens for the bench and show how to rotate them via the Console.

[11:44] Sonia: Ok, great — sounds like we have the high-level plan. A few small Qs: 1) Can you run an end-to-end bench that includes mobile network sim? 2) Will you share the script to validate JSON schema enforcement? 3) How soon can we get a demo app that shows function calling + structured output?

[12:05] Priya: 1) Yes — we can integrate network emulation during stress tests. 2) We'll include the schema validator script in the repo. 3) Demo app and example repo will be sent with SDK snippets; aim for 48-72 hours.

[12:20] Eli: To recap next steps: Redwood will send the benchmark template, perf spreadsheet, SDK snippets, and draft SOW. Zenith will send traces and confirm infra contact. Schedule the baseline bench for week of 05/19.

[12:38] Marcus: Sounds good. One last thing — who do we loop in for procurement if pilot goes well?

[12:44] Eli: I'll include sales ops and a procurement contact in the follow-up email. We can provide a standard pilot contract and then go to reserved capacity discussions.

[12:56] Sonia: Thanks everyone.

[13:00] Eli: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts. End call.

Notes / transcript quirks: occasional mis-transcriptions — 'OpenAI compat' appears as 'open eye comp' in places; 'KV cache' sometimes 'K V cash'; small crosstalk at 03:15 and 09:24.
